summary: EXP-002 improves over EXP-001 by expanding to 510 cases, adding splits, repo-derived and cross-program claims, external controls, adversarial promotions, hard positives, hard negatives, multiple baselines, transition-level labeling, and severity-weighted recall. It remains non-publication-grade because labels are script-generated, not blind-reviewed, and metadata baselines solve the task by construction.
blocking_issues: Needs EXP-FRONTIER-003 with 300+ fresh cases, at least 30% external/cross-project, 100+ real LLM/research-agent outputs, no model-visible layer labels, two or more independent annotators, inter-annotator agreement, locked splits, and serious baselines.

summary: A strong venue would reject EXP-002 as an internally expanded benchmark with construct leakage. Metadata-free scores are more honest and promising, but no blind labels, inter-annotator agreement, external baselines, or real previously unseen outputs exist yet.
blocking_issues: Needs metadata-free detector on locked held-out real claims from previously unseen artifact-derived research outputs, blind labels from at least three reviewers, strong severity-weighted recall on blocking errors, and gains over lexical, LLM-judge, SHACL/type-style, and provenance baselines.
